payload.task_text:
You are an inventory manager responsible for monitoring product stock levels and coordinating restocking activities for an online store. Your goal is to analyze the current product inventory, forecast demand, generate reports, and ensure timely restock scheduling.

Start by reading the Inventory_Policy.pdf in your workspace, which describes the reorder thresholds and lead time expectations. Also review the warehouse_config.json file that contains warehouse capacity limits and supplier contact information.

Query the e-commerce platform to retrieve the complete product catalog. For each product, gather the product name, category, regular price, stock quantity, stock status, and total sales count. You will use this data to assess inventory health and compute reorder priorities.

Write a Python script called demand_forecast.py in your workspace and execute it using command-line tools. The script should compute a simple demand velocity metric for each product by dividing total sales by an assumed 180-day selling period to get daily sales rate. Then calculate days of supply by dividing current stock quantity by the daily sales rate (use 999 for products with zero sales rate). Determine a reorder point for each product as 14 times the daily sales rate (representing a 14-day lead time buffer). Flag products as Critical urgency if their current stock is at or below the reorder point and they are not out of stock, flag out-of-stock products as Out_of_Stock urgency, and flag all others as Normal.

Create an Excel workbook called Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx in your workspace with four sheets.

The first sheet should be named Product_Inventory and contain columns for product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, and days_of_supply. Include one row for every product in the catalog, sorted by days_of_supply ascending so the most urgent items appear first.

The second sheet should be named Reorder_Alerts and contain columns for product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, and urgency. Include only the products that have Critical or Out_of_Stock urgency, sorted by urgency with Out_of_Stock items first.

The third sheet should be named Category_Summary and contain columns for category, product_count, avg_stock, and total_value. Total value should be the sum of price times stock quantity for each product in the category. Include one row per product category.

The fourth sheet should be named Restock_Schedule and contain columns for product_name, reorder_date, quantity, and supplier. For each Critical or Out_of_Stock product, set the reorder date to March 10, 2026. The quantity to order should be the reorder point minus current stock (minimum 1 unit). The supplier should be "Primary Supplier" for all items.

Publish the Category_Summary data to the shared spreadsheet system so the team can view real-time inventory status. Create a spreadsheet titled "Inventory Dashboard" with a sheet containing the category summary data.

Schedule a restock review meeting on the shared calendar for March 11, 2026 at 10:00 AM lasting one hour. The event summary should be "Inventory Restock Review Meeting" and the description should mention the number of critical items identified.

Send an email to purchasing@company.com with the subject "Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required" summarizing the number of out-of-stock and critical products, along with the top three most urgent items that need immediate restocking.
Note: Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes every source fact and computed metric into one canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of two parallel coder sub-agents (workbook writer and external-services writer). No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the two writer contracts below are the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Inventory_Policy.pdf and warehouse_config.json, and freeze their thresholds and supplier facts. Retrieve the complete WooCommerce catalog with woo_products_list(page=1,perPage=100), continuing only when pagination requires it, and retrieve complete categories. Require 82 unique live product IDs, preserve every category membership plus literal regular_price, stock_quantity, stock_status and total_sales, and use full_output_path if the response is oversized. Write and run demand_forecast.py: daily_sales=total_sales/180; days_supply=stock/daily_sales or 999 for zero-rate products; reorder_point=14*daily_sales; urgency Out_of_Stock first, then Critical when stock<=reorder_point, else Normal; order_qty=reorder_point-stock (minimum 1 unit) with reorder_date 2026-03-10 and supplier "Primary Supplier". Read the script and its output back, then freeze one canonical inventory_metrics.json in the workspace containing: the full 82-row inventory list sorted by days_of_supply ascending, the Reorder_Alerts rows (Critical and Out_of_Stock only, Out_of_Stock items first), the Category_Summary rows (category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value=regular_price*stock), the Restock_Schedule rows, and the top-three most urgent items with complete product names plus the out-of-stock and critical counts. This file is the single binding input for both sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the store, the PDF, the config, or the script.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming inventory_metrics.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly four sheets: Product_Inventory with columns product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, days_of_supply and all 82 rows sorted by days_of_supply ascending; Reorder_Alerts with columns product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, urgency and only Critical/Out_of_Stock rows, Out_of_Stock first; Category_Summary with columns category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value, one row per category; Restock_Schedule with columns product_name, reorder_date, quantity, supplier and the frozen March 10, 2026 rows. Write literal values only, read all four populated ranges back, and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External-services writer — sole owner of the three external outputs. Fully paginate the exact-title search for cloud spreadsheet Inventory Dashboard, create/reuse at most once, block duplicate titles/tabs, own exactly one Category_Summary tab, batch-write the frozen category rows and read them back; search the exact Inventory Restock Review Meeting on 2026-03-11 10:00-11:00 America/New_York, create at most once with the frozen critical-item count in the description, and get_event; paginate Sent search/read candidates for purchasing@company.com and exact subject Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required, send at most once with the frozen out-of-stock/critical counts and the top three complete item names, then read it back.

After Wave 1, verify both handoffs in one single pass (never per-branch iteration) against inventory_metrics.json: workbook cell-for-cell, dashboard rows, event identity and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

nodes.text:
You are the workbook writer for an inventory lifecycle report. Your sole deliverable is an Excel workbook built EXACTLY from a frozen data payload. Do NOT recompute anything, do NOT read the store/PDF/config/script — the JSON payload is the single binding source of truth.

CONTEXT
- Workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace
- Frozen payload file: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace/inventory_metrics.json
- Output file (create exactly once): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace/Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx

PAYLOAD STRUCTURE (read it with mcp filesystem read_text_file)
- payload["product_inventory"]: list of 82 dicts, each with keys product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, days_of_supply — ALREADY SORTED by days_of_supply ascending.
- payload["reorder_alerts"]: list of 29 dicts with keys product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, urgency — ALREADY SORTED with Out_of_Stock first, then Critical.
- payload["category_summary"]: list of 8 dicts with keys category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value.
- payload["restock_schedule"]: list of 29 dicts with keys product_name, reorder_date, quantity, supplier.

WORKBOOK SPEC (4 sheets, exact names, header row + data rows, literal values ONLY — no formulas):
1. Sheet "Product_Inventory": header row [product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, days_of_supply] followed by all 82 rows from payload["product_inventory"] in the given order.
2. Sheet "Reorder_Alerts": header row [product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, urgency] followed by all 29 rows from payload["reorder_alerts"] in the given order.
3. Sheet "Category_Summary": header row [category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value] followed by all 8 rows from payload["category_summary"] in the given order.
4. Sheet "Restock_Schedule": header row [product_name, reorder_date, quantity, supplier] followed by all 29 rows from payload["restock_schedule"] in the given order.

BUILD STEPS (use the excel MCP tools; file path as above):
1. Use create_workbook to create the file, then rename the default sheet to "Product_Inventory" (or create/rename worksheets so the workbook contains exactly these four sheets in this order: Product_Inventory, Reorder_Alerts, Category_Summary, Restock_Schedule). Use create_worksheet + rename_worksheet as needed; delete any leftover default sheet (e.g., "Sheet") so there are exactly 4 sheets.
2. For each sheet, write the header row plus all data rows starting at A1 using write_data_to_excel (list of lists: each sublist is a row). Preserve values exactly as in the JSON (numbers as numbers, strings as strings, e.g. price 42.17, days_of_supply 0.0 or 999, reorder_date "2026-03-10", supplier "Primary Supplier").
3. After writing, read back EVERY populated range (read_data_from_excel) and verify cell-by-cell that each sheet's values equal the payload arrays (row counts: 83, 30, 9, 30 including headers).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (all must pass):
- File exists at the exact output path; exactly 4 sheets named/ordered Product_Inventory, Reorder_Alerts, Category_Summary, Restock_Schedule.
- Product_Inventory has 82 data rows (83 incl. header) matching payload["product_inventory"] exactly and in order.
- Reorder_Alerts has 29 data rows matching payload["reorder_alerts"] exactly and in order (Out_of_Stock first).
- Category_Summary has 8 data rows matching payload["category_summary"] exactly.
- Restock_Schedule has 29 data rows matching payload["restock_schedule"] exactly.
- No formulas, only literal values; no extra sheets, no extra columns/rows.

RETURN (report back): the absolute output path, the sheet order as verified, the row count of each sheet (incl. header), and for each sheet a statement of whether the read-back matched the payload (list any mismatches explicitly if found). If any check fails, fix the workbook and re-verify before returning.
Build Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx

You are the external-workflow operator for an inventory alert workflow. You own EXACTLY three external outputs: a Google Spreadsheet dashboard, a Google Calendar event, and an alert email. All content comes from a frozen JSON payload — do NOT recompute anything and do NOT read the store/PDF/config/script.

CONTEXT
- Workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace
- Frozen payload file: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace/inventory_metrics.json (read with mcp filesystem read_text_file)

KEY PAYLOAD FACTS (already verified by the parent agent — use verbatim):
- payload["counts"] = {"total_products": 82, "out_of_stock": 5, "critical": 24, "normal": 53}
- payload["category_summary"]: 8 dicts with keys category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value (e.g. {"category": "TV & Home Theater", "product_count": 13, "avg_stock": 12.77, "total_value": 68250.21}, ...)
- payload["top_three_most_urgent"]: 3 dicts with keys product_name, urgency, current_stock, reorder_point, days_of_supply. The three product names are: (1) "Silencer Panels, Flame Retardant Sound‑Absorption, Polyester Fiber Stable for Recording Studio Home Theater Black", (2) "30kg digital scale for shop and kitchen green display 72hrs battery back up and Back Light", (3) "TYPE-C Earphone for OnePlus 8 Pro , OnePlus Eight Pro in Ear Type C Wired Earphones with Mic, Braided 1.2 Metre Cable, Met...". Use the EXACT full names from the JSON file when composing the email body.

TASK 1 — Google Spreadsheet dashboard (create at most once, no duplicates):
1. Search for a spreadsheet titled "Inventory Dashboard": call search_spreadsheets(query="Inventory Dashboard") and also list_spreadsheets() to confirm. Currently none exists (parent verified), but re-check; if one already exists with the exact title and a Category_Summary tab, REUSE it (do not create a second one).
2. If none exists, create exactly one: create_spreadsheet(title="Inventory Dashboard"). It will contain a default sheet — rename it to "Category_Summary" (rename_sheet or batch_update). Ensure the spreadsheet has EXACTLY ONE tab named "Category_Summary" (delete/avoid any extra default tab if present).
3. Write into the Category_Summary tab: header row [category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value] in row 1, then the 8 payload rows starting at A2 (update_cells or batch_update_cells). Literal values only.
4. Read the tab back (get_sheet_data) and verify all 9 rows match the payload exactly.

TASK 2 — Google Calendar event (create at most once):
1. List events between 2026-03-11T00:00:00-05:00 and 2026-03-11T23:59:59-05:00 (list_events with timeMin/timeMax) and search for an event with summary "Inventory Restock Review Meeting". None exists (parent verified); re-check, and if it already exists, do NOT create a duplicate — report its id.
2. If none exists, create exactly one event:
   - summary: "Inventory Restock Review Meeting"
   - start: dateTime "2026-03-11T10:00:00", timeZone "America/New_York"
   - end:   dateTime "2026-03-11T11:00:00", timeZone "America/New_York"
   - description: a sentence that explicitly mentions the number of critical items identified, e.g. "Review of 24 critical inventory items identified by demand forecasting. Agenda: restock scheduling, supplier coordination, and stock level review." (must contain the number 24 from payload["counts"]["critical"]).
3. Verify with get_event on the returned event id: summary, start/end times, and description contain "24".

TASK 3 — Alert email (send at most once):
1. Check the Sent folder (search_emails in folder "Sent" / "INBOX.Sent" / "SENT" — check which folder the mail server uses by listing folders) for subject "Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required" sent to purchasing@company.com. None exists (parent verified); if one already exists, do NOT send again — report its id.
2. If none exists, send exactly one email:
   - to: purchasing@company.com
   - subject: "Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required"
   - body (plain text): summarize that 5 products are out of stock and 24 products are at critical stock levels, and list the top three most urgent items requiring immediate restocking with their EXACT full product names (from payload["top_three_most_urgent"]), e.g.:
     "Inventory Alert: 5 product(s) are currently OUT OF STOCK and 24 product(s) are at CRITICAL stock levels (at or below reorder point). Immediate restocking is required for the following top 3 most urgent items: 1) <name1> 2) <name2> 3) <name3>."
3. Verify the email was sent by reading it back from the Sent folder (search or list the sent folder; confirm recipient, subject, and that the body contains the counts 5 and 24 and the three names).

CONSTRAINTS:
- No recomputation; copy values verbatim from inventory_metrics.json.
- Create at most one spreadsheet/event/email; never duplicate titles/tabs/events/emails.
- For all calendar events use timezone America/New_York.

RETURN (report back): the spreadsheet id + title + tab name + row count written/verified; the calendar event id + summary + start/end + description; the email id + recipient + subject (and confirmation the body contains the required counts and the three top item names). Report any mismatch found and fix before returning.
External services: sheet, calendar, email
